newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals dip on firm yen, weak spot.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals dip on firm yen, weak spot.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended lower across the board on Wednesday, weighed down by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar and weak bullion prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from seven yen to 14 yen per gram lower. Benchmark April was off 13 yen at 1,372 yen.

"Although the yen's firmer tone has poured cold water on sentiment in the gold futures market, private investors were tending to hunt for bargains most of the day after taking profits on Tuesday," an analyst at a commodity brokerage said.
Spot bullion was quoted at $340.35/65 per ounce at 0730 GMT, against $340.30/80 in New York on Tuesday.
In the bullion market, buying by Japanese traders was matched by selling from Australian producers, dealers said.

"Buying by Japanese traders in arbitrage dealings was countered by hedge selling by Australian producers," one trader said. He said spot gold sentiment remained weak on lingering concern over possible gold sales by European central banks.
Platinum and palladium futures were directionless, with private investors quick to take advantage of price dips to cover short positions, while trade houses were generally buying.

Some traders said rumours have circulated the precious metal industry that a Russian trade mission will visit Japan later this month after a long delay, to negotiate the renewal of export contracts for platinum group metals (PGM).
They said the PGM industry has not yet received a formal notice from Russia.
Platinum futures ranged from five to 12 yen per gram weaker. Benchmark April closed down seven at 1,465 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from three to nine yen per gram down, with benchmark April finishing down four at 600 yen.
Benchmark April silver was off 2.7 yen at 193.0 yen.
